questions.q: On what date did India officially gain its independence from British rule?
questions.a: August 15, 1947. A wrong answer here suggests a lack of awareness of the most fundamental date in modern Indian history, requiring a review of the basic timeline of the freedom struggle.

questions.q: Why did the Muslim League, led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah, demand a separate country?
questions.a: They argued that Muslims were a separate nation and required their own land to protect their interests. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks it was only about British policy, ignoring the internal political demands made by Indian groups.

questions.q: If you were a leader in the Congress party in 1947, how would you explain the decision to accept partition?
questions.a: Steps: 1. Acknowledge the goal of freedom. 2. Recognize the deadlock between the Muslim League and Congress. 3. Conclude that partition was the "price" to end British colonial rule quickly. A wrong answer here shows the student fails to understand the concept of "compromise" in political negotiations.

questions.q: Compare the roles of the British government and the Indian political parties in the events of 1947.
questions.a: The British (under Attlee) announced they would leave, while the Congress and the Muslim League had to decide how the country would be structured. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks Britain forced the partition, ignoring the active political demands made by the Muslim League and the eventual acceptance by the Congress.

questions.q: Was the partition of India considered a simple or a complex decision by the leaders of that time? Justify your answer.
questions.a: It was a complex, difficult decision because it was seen as the "price of independence," meaning it was a painful trade-off. A wrong answer indicates the student views history as a series of simple events rather than difficult human and political choices.

questions.q: If India had not been partitioned, what do you think would have been the biggest challenge for the new government?
questions.a: The answer should focus on the difficulty of governing a nation where major political groups disagreed on the fundamental structure of the state. A poor answer ignores the political conflict and focuses only on geography or resources.
